title: Facelift, Neck Lift & Blepharoplasty in Istanbul: Stay Duration & Privacy
seoTitle: Facelift & Eyelid Surgery in Istanbul: Stay & Privacy (2026)
metaDescription: Plan your facelift, neck lift, or blepharoplasty stay in Istanbul with realistic recovery days, stitch timelines, and private hotel logistics.
quickAnswer: Most international patients need 10 to 14 days in Istanbul for a deep-plane facelift or neck lift, and 7 to 10 days for standalone eyelid surgery. That window covers hospital discharge, initial swelling, suture removal, and surgeon clearance before flying. body.text: How many days in Istanbul do deep-plane facelift vs eyelid surgery require?

Plan 10 to 14 nights in Istanbul for a deep-plane facelift or combined face and neck lift, compared with 7 to 10 nights for upper or lower blepharoplasty alone. According to [ISAPS surgery-abroad guidance](https://www.isaps.org/discover/patients-home/considering-your-procedure-abroad/make-a-plan/), patients should remain near their operating team for at least one week, with deeper facial work requiring extra monitoring days.

Standalone upper blepharoplasty is often a day-case procedure, whereas deep-plane facelift and platysmaplasty typically involve one to two nights in hospital followed by clinic checks on days two, five, and ten. Combining eyelid surgery with a facelift extends early swelling, so your stay should follow the longest recovery curve.
When are stitches removed and when does bruising settle enough for travel?

Eyelid stitches are usually removed between days 5 and 7, while facelift and neck lift sutures or staples come out between days 7 and 14 unless dissolvable closures are used, per [NHS facelift guidance](https://www.nhs.uk/tests-and-treatments/cosmetic-procedures/cosmetic-surgery/facelift/) and [ISAPS upper blepharoplasty guidance](https://www.isaps.org/discover/patients-home/procedures/face-head-procedures/upper-blepharoplasty/). Bruising peaks around days 3 to 4 and typically softens enough for discreet travel by day 10 to 14.

Per [American Society of Plastic Surgeons recovery milestones](https://www.plasticsurgery.org/news/blog/your-facelift-recovery-explained-from-day-1-to-day-30), tightness and yellow-green residual bruising often linger past week two even after incisions close cleanly. [NHS eyelid surgery guidance](https://www.nhs.uk/tests-and-treatments/cosmetic-procedures/cosmetic-surgery/eyelid-surgery/) recommends keeping your head propped upright on extra pillows during the first days, using cold compresses as instructed, and wearing UV sunglasses outdoors to shield healing skin from wind and glare.

items: Written fit-to-fly clearance issued by your operating surgeon after final incision inspection.
All non-dissolvable sutures, clips, and drains removed and documented in your discharge summary.
Prescribed eye drops, ointments, and oral medications packed in carry-on with pharmacy labels.
Wide-brimmed hat, wraparound sunglasses, and loose zip-front tops ready for airport transit.
Airline wheelchair or buggy assistance booked at least 48 hours before departure.

How do you evaluate natural, non-overpulled surgeon portfolios?

Evaluate a facial surgeon's portfolio by examining unedited, standardized before-and-after sets taken at 6 to 12 months post-op under identical lighting, head angle, and neutral facial expression. Look closely at earlobes, tragus contours, hairline temples, and neck bands rather than heavily filtered front-facing social media clips.

Overpulled results often show stretched "pixie" earlobes, flattened cheeks, visible pre-auricular scars, or a swept corner of the mouth. Ask to see multiple patients matching your age bracket, skin elasticity, and neck anatomy, and review formal risk disclosures such as the [BAAPS facelift consent framework](https://baaps.org.uk/_userfiles/pages/files/procedures/baaps_facelift_updated_may_24.pdf), which outlines nicotine risks, scar placement, and separate hospital, anesthesia, and surgeon fees.

faq.q: How soon after a facelift in Istanbul can I fly home?
faq.a: Most surgeons clear short-haul flights around day 10 to 14 after a deep-plane facelift, once drains and stitches are out and swelling is stable. Long-haul flights may require a longer stay depending on your individual clotting risk and your surgeon's assessment.

faq.q: Can I walk around Istanbul after eyelid surgery?
faq.a: Light, flat walking inside your hotel or along quiet shaded streets is usually encouraged within a few days to support circulation, but avoid strenuous sightseeing, heat, hammams, and bending over for at least two weeks unless your surgeon clears you earlier.

faq.q: Will hotel staff know I had facial surgery?
faq.a: Experienced Istanbul luxury and boutique hotels host medical travelers routinely and maintain strict guest privacy. We request discreet check-in, private corridor rooms away from elevators, and contactless room service delivery so you can rest undisturbed.

faq.q: Should I bring a travel companion for a facelift trip?
faq.a: Yes. Having a trusted companion during the first 48 to 72 hours helps with medication timing, cold compresses, meals, and clinic transfers. If you travel solo, we can coordinate licensed private nursing visits at your hotel.

faq.q: What should I wear for the flight home after facial surgery?
faq.a: Choose button-down or zip-front shirts that do not pull over your face or ears, loose comfortable trousers, slip-on shoes, and wraparound sunglasses. Keep prescribed ointments and saline sprays in a clear carry-on pouch.
